{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-tn","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4917046c7bc6137e4767a1a68daa8ff372f4015f129fd4ef0a978a737405a1cb","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","source_liveness_sha256":"d27b9a94f03ec29d960b8eea38966606a7d3fdb703ad30b19ecd93f9bc70d0c7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving responsibilities","heading":"C — Driving responsibilities: the Problem Driver Pointer System, losing your license, surrender and hearings, address changes, the Non-Resident Violator Compact, the point system, restricted licenses, medical review, financial responsibility, reporting crashes and what to do at a crash scene","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driving responsibilities: the Problem Driver Pointer System, losing your license, surrender and hearings, address changes, the Non-Resident Violator Compact, the point system, restricted licenses, medical review, financial responsibility, reporting crashes and what to do at a crash scene
Knowledge domain: the duties that come with a Tennessee license — how out-of-state problems block a license, what gets a license suspended or revoked, how surrender, hearings and address changes work, how points add up toward suspension, when a restricted license is possible, how medical conditions are reviewed, what proof of financial responsibility means, when and how crashes must be reported, and how to act at a crash scene.

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Before issuing a license, Tennessee uses the Problem Driver Pointer System to search the National Driver Register, a national file of problem drivers reported by all 51 U.S. jurisdictions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
If the search shows you have an unresolved problem in another state, Tennessee cannot issue you a license, even a renewal, until that state's matter is cleared. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Examiners can only tell you which state reported a problem and give a phone number for it; for details you must contact that state, because Tennessee does not hold them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
A Tennessee license may be revoked or suspended for DUI, including refusing a blood alcohol test under implied consent. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Letting someone else use your license or ID, or fraudulently altering a license, can cost you your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
Leaving the scene of a crash that injures or kills someone, or failing to stop and give aid, is grounds for losing your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Two reckless driving violations within 12 months, or drag racing, can lead to suspension or revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
Driving away from a gas station without paying for fuel is grounds for losing your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
Failing to show proof of insurance or financial responsibility to an officer after a crash or a moving violation charge can lead to suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
A driver under 18 can lose driving privileges for any drug or alcohol conviction, whether or not it happened while driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
A driver under 18 can lose driving privileges for dropping out of school, failing to make satisfactory progress in school, or carrying weapons on school property. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A01
A suspended or revoked license must be turned in to the Department of Safety within 20 days, and failing to surrender it brings a $75 fine on top of other fines and costs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A01
Before suspending, revoking or canceling a license, the department notifies the driver in writing and offers a hearing, except in cases of final judgments and convictions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A02
You must report a new address to the Department of Safety within 10 days, and you can do it online, by letter or with a form at any Driver License Service Center. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A02
Under the Non-Resident Violator Compact, if you ignore a traffic citation from Tennessee or another member state, your driving privileges will be suspended, revoked or canceled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
A compact suspension lasts until the court tells the department that the citation has been properly handled and the fees are paid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
Every traffic violation or crash on your Department of Safety record carries a point value, based on court reports and officers' crash reports. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
An adult driver aged 18 or older who builds up 12 or more points within 12 months receives a notice of proposed suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
An adult driver with 6 to 11 points within any 12 months is mailed an advisory letter as a warning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
A juvenile driver under 18 who builds up 6 or more points within 12 months receives a notice of proposed suspension, and one with 1 to 5 points is mailed an advisory letter. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
A Defensive Driving Course can help you avoid a point suspension or shorten it, but that option is available only once in any five-year period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A02
After a suspension for frequent violations, you must pay reinstatement fees and file proof of insurance, with SR-22 insurance required for adults, before getting your regular license back. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A02
Driving while your license is suspended extends the suspension and can lead to criminal prosecution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A02
A restricted license lets a driver whose license was suspended or revoked, but who needs to drive for work or school, drive only for the specific purposes written on it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A03
Passing a stopped school, church or youth bus that is loading or unloading passengers carries 8 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A03
Failing to stop at a railroad crossing carries 8 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A03
Reckless driving carries 6 points, and careless or negligent driving carries 4 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A03
Using a cell phone while driving under age 18 carries 6 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A03
Failing to yield to emergency vehicles, or failing to change lanes or slow down for authorized vehicles on the roadside, carries 6 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A03
Contributing to a crash that causes property damage carries 3 points, one that causes bodily injury 4 points, and one that causes another person's death 8 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A04
A DUI restricted license is not available to a driver with a prior DUI or adult driving while impaired conviction within 10 years, or a prior vehicular homicide, aggravated vehicular homicide or vehicular assault. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A04
When the department learns that a physical or mental condition affects someone's driving, that driver must send a doctor's medical report within 30 days of being notified. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A04
A driver who loses consciousness or control from epilepsy, cardiac syncope, diabetes or a similar condition must be suspended and stay episode-free for at least six months before reinstatement. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A04
A driver whose ability is in question may be told to take a full or partial driver examination, and ignoring a request for an exam or medical report brings a suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A04
Liability insurance covers damage you cause to others, collision insurance covers damage to your own vehicle, and uninsured motorist insurance covers damage caused by uninsured drivers. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A04
Collision insurance is not required in Tennessee, but the Financial Responsibility Law requires you to show proof of financial responsibility whenever you are charged with a violation or are in a crash, whoever was at fault. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F37 | anchor: A05
Being convicted of failing to show proof of financial responsibility suspends your driving privileges and blocks renewal of your vehicle tags and registration. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F38 | anchor: A05
You must immediately notify local police, or the county sheriff or nearest Highway Patrol outside a city, of any crash causing death, injury or property damage over $50. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F39 | anchor: A05
A crash that kills or injures anyone, or damages any one person's property by more than $400, is a reportable crash that must be reported to the Department of Safety. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F40 | anchor: A05
The driver or owner in a reportable crash must file an Owner/Driver Report with the Department of Safety within 20 days, regardless of who was at fault. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F41 | anchor: A05
Tennessee law requires drivers in a crash to stop immediately at or as near the scene as possible without blocking traffic, and to turn off the ignition to prevent a fire. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F42 | anchor: A05
Do not move an injured person from a wrecked vehicle unless you have medical or rescue training or there is immediate danger such as fire. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F43 | anchor: A06
If you come upon a crash and are not trained to give aid, call 911 and keep driving slowly past so you do not get in the way of police and rescue crews or cause a secondary collision. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0104]

Misconceptions: Tennessee cannot tell you the details of another state's report; points are not the only way to lose a license, since many single offenses also trigger suspension; collision insurance is optional but proof of financial responsibility is not; the duty to report a crash does not depend on who caused it; stopping to stare at a crash scene is not helpful.
Mnemonics: surrender in twenty, move in ten; twelve points for adults, six for teens; fifty dollars to call police, four hundred to report to the state, twenty days to file.
Glossary: Problem Driver Pointer System means the tool that checks the national register of problem drivers; restricted license means a license limited to stated purposes such as work or school; SR-22 means an insurer's filing that proves liability coverage; reportable crash means one the Department of Safety must receive a written report for.
Dynamic facts: point values, fines, the surrender deadline, reporting dollar thresholds, the Defensive Driving Course limit and restricted license rules are set by Tennessee law and policy and can change; confirm them on official Tennessee sources before showing them to learners.
